title: WPSS/1900/2025 of RAMESH CHANDRA SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPSS 1900/2025
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Ms. Prabha Naithani, Advocate, for
the petitioner.
Mr. Ganesh Datt Kandpal, Deputy
AG, for the State.
(2) Petitioner was offered
compassionate appointment on Group 'D'
post of Peon, vide order dated 30.5.2006,
passed by District Education Officer (Basic),
Almora. He thereafter staked claim for
appointment on a Group 'C' post of Junior
Clerk on the ground that he is qualified for
such appointment and one similarly situate
person was offered appointment as Group
'C' employee. The claim staked by the
petitioner has been rejected by the District
Education Officer (Basic), vide order dated
5.10.2023. Thus feeling aggrieved,
petitioner has approached this Court.
(3) Learned Counsel for the petitioner
submits that petitioner's father was
employed as Assistant Teacher, Govt.
Primary School, who died on 25.1.2006.
Petitioner, who was qualified for
appointment on a Group 'C' post, made
application in which he sought appointment
as Group 'C' employee, however instead of
giving appointment as Junior Clerk,
petitioner was offered appointment as Peon.
She submits that a similarly situate person,
whose father was also serving as Assistant
Teacher, Govt. Primary School, was given
compassionate appointment after death of
his father on the post of Junior Clerk, vide
order dated 4.3.2006. Thus she submits
that it is a case of discrimination. She also
refers to a letter issued by Regional

Additional Director, Elementary, Kumaon to
District Education Officer, Elementary on
5.10.2023 in support of her contention that
the competent authority was not informed
about the post for which petitioner had
applied.
(4) Learned State Counsel, per
contra, submits that after accepting
appointment on a Group 'D' post in 2006,
petitioner cannot now stake claim for
upgrading the post offered to her on
compassionate ground from Group 'D' to
Group 'C'. He submits that after accepting
appointment on a Group 'D' post, petitioner
is estopped from raising any further claim
for upgradation of the post. He further
submits that although rules provide for
compassionate appointment to dependants
of deceased government servant in
deserving cases, however the said rules do
not provide a hereditary right of
appointment. He submits that
compassionate appointment is an exception
to the general rule that selection has to be
merit based. He submits that if petitioner is
more qualified and he thinks that the post
offered to him is not commensurate with
his status, qualification and experience,
then he can apply for appointment to a
suitable post in open market; face
competition and once selected, he can join
a higher post.
(5) This Court finds substance in the
submission made by learned State Counsel.
After having accepted appointment on
Group 'D' post, that too in 2006, petitioner
cannot now turn around and stake claim for
appointment on Group 'C' post. Learned
State Counsel is right in submitting that
compassionate appointment cannot be
claimed as a matter of course and there are

various aspects which are to be considered
while giving compassionate appointment. It
is also well settled that compassionate
appointment is given to a dependant family
member of the deceased employee to help
the family tide over the sudden financial
crisis, which befalls upon it on account of
death of the sole bread earner.
(6) Petitioner has served for nearly
two decades as Group 'D' employee,
therefore he cannot now be permitted to
stake claim for appointment on a Group 'C'
post, that too on compassionate ground.
(7) For the reasons aforesaid, writ
petition fails and is dismissed.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
13.11.2025
